plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded three-dimensional cutaway drawing of a domed room built as a half-ellipsoid on a circular base. The outer shell carries a blue-to-white gradient and is cut away at the front so the viewer looks into the interior, where the inner surface and the floor are shaded warm tan; a thick gray band forms the base slab beneath the floor. Two small dark points on the floor mark the foci, labeled F' on the left and F on the right. A fan of dark blue segments with arrowheads leaves F', rises at a range of angles to strike the inside of the curved dome at several separated points, and reflects back down, every one arriving at F. The paths cross one another mid-room, and no two share a bounce point. Drawing many distinct routes between the same pair of labeled points emphasizes that the convergence holds no matter which direction a ray sets out in. The illustration accounts for the acoustics of a whispering chamber, where a person speaking softly at one focus of an elliptical dome is heard clearly by a listener at the other.

elements: Half-ellipsoid dome shell, cut away across the front so the interior is visible
Outer surface of the dome with blue-to-white vertical gradient (deep blue at the rim, pale blue/white near the top)
Thin white/light highlight band along the cut rim showing the shell thickness
Inner surface of the dome shaded warm tan, visible through the cutaway
Horizontal shading band (tonal break) circling the inside of the dome about one-third up
Elliptical/circular floor disk of the room, warm tan with a light-to-dark gradient
Thick gray cylindrical base slab beneath the floor
Focus point F' — small dark blue dot on the left of the floor, on the major axis
Focus point F — small dark blue dot on the right of the floor, on the major axis
Text label "F'" below-left of the left focus, "F" below-right of the right focus
Seven dark navy outbound ray segments leaving F' at different upward angles
Seven dark navy return ray segments from each dome bounce point down to F
Arrowheads at the midpoint of each segment indicating direction of travel (up-and-away from F', down-and-toward F)
Distinct reflection (bounce) points spread across the inner dome surface, no two rays sharing one
Crossing pattern of rays in the middle of the room

interactions.teaches: The room is a solid half-ellipsoid, not a flat ellipse: the foci sit on the floor and every reflection happens on a curved 3D surface, yet the focus-to-focus property holds from any viewing angle.
Picking one launch direction isolates its single bounce point and its return leg, showing that this particular angle — steep or shallow — still lands exactly on F.
Switching from one highlighted route to the full fan reveals that the convergence at F is systematic for every launch angle, not a coincidence of the chosen ray.
interactions.label: Rays shown

interactions.teaches: Pulses leaving F' in all directions travel equal total path lengths (2a), so they bounce once off the dome and arrive back at F together — the whispering-chamber effect.
interactions.label: Play sound pulses from F'

demo_steps.title: One whisper, one path
demo_steps.narration: A single ray leaves F' at a steep angle, strikes the inside of the dome once, and comes straight back down to F. Click any other ray to change which route is shown.

demo_steps.title: A different launch angle
demo_steps.narration: Choosing a shallower ray moves the bounce point far to the side, yet the reflected segment still terminates exactly at F — the reflection angle at the curved wall always redirects the ray to the other focus.

demo_steps.title: The whole fan
demo_steps.narration: All seven rays at once: they leave F' in a spread of directions, bounce at seven separate points on the dome, cross one another mid-room, and every single one arrives at F.

demo_steps.title: Sound in motion
demo_steps.narration: Playing the pulses shows why the listener hears a whisper clearly: each path has the same total length 2a, so the sound reassembles at F at the same instant.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes: +X screen-right (major axis of the room), +Y up, +Z toward viewer (depth). Dome = upper half of an ellipsoid with semi-axes a=3.0 in X, c=3.0 in Z, b=2.0 in Y, centered at origin; floor is the disk y=0, x²/9+z²/9≤1. Shell drawn with ~0.08 thickness; the front half (z>0 region in front of the cut plane z≈+1.1) is removed so the interior is visible. Gray base slab: cylinder radius 3.15, height 0.45, centered at y=−0.22, color #57585a with a lighter top lip #8d8e90. Floor tan gradient #f2e2bf (near) to #dcc79b (far). Dome outer gradient: deep blue #1f6ab0 at the rim rising to pale blue #b9dcf2 then near-white #f4fbff at the crown; cut-rim highlight strip #ffffff/#e8f2fa. Dome inner surface tan #e3cfa4 with a darker tonal band #cdb888 running horizontally around the interior at about y=0.7. Foci lie in the vertical XY cross-section (z=0) of the ellipse x²/9+y²/4=1: focal distance sqrt(9−4)=2.236, so F' at (−2.236, 0.02, 0) and F at (+2.236, 0.02, 0), drawn as dark navy dots radius ~0.09. Labels 'F'' and 'F' in italic serif, ~0.35 units below/outside each dot. Rays: all seven lie in the z=0 vertical plane and are dark navy #1c4e80, line width ~3px, with a single solid arrowhead at the midpoint of each segment. Each ray leaves F' at an upward angle, hits the ellipse boundary at a point P, and returns to F; total path |F'P|+|PF| = 2a = 6 for every ray (the defining ellipse property). Use seven well-separated bounce points on the ellipse, roughly at parameter angles t = 25°, 55°, 80°, 100°, 125°, 150°, 168° measured counterclockwise from +X on x=3cos t, y=2sin t — giving bounces spread from the right shoulder, over the crown, to the left shoulder so the outbound and return legs cross in the middle of the room, matching the source's woven crossing pattern.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the dome as two nested half-ellipsoid meshes (outer with THREE.BackSide off, inner with side=BackSide so the interior is lit) plus a thin torus-like rim strip along the cut; use a vertical gradient via a ShaderMaterial or a 1D CanvasTexture mapped to Y for both the blue exterior and the tan interior. Cut away the front with a clipping plane (renderer.localClippingEnabled = true, THREE.Plane normal (0,0,-1) at z=1.1) applied to the shell materials only, so the floor and rays stay whole. Rays as Line2/LineSegments2 for constant screen-space width; arrowheads as small flat cone meshes or sprite triangles oriented along each segment. Hit-testing for click: use invisible fat cylinders along each outbound segment as raycast proxies. All-rays view draws all seven at full opacity; single-ray view dims the others to ~12% opacity rather than hiding them so the fan context is retained. Animation: a small emissive sphere per ray advancing along the polyline at constant speed with all pulses sharing one normalized time parameter (path length identical), so they visibly reconverge at F simultaneously; add a soft expanding ring pulse at F' on launch and at F on arrival. Keep labels as HTML/CSS2DRenderer overlays anchored to the focus dots so they stay upright while orbiting. Lighting: hemisphere light plus one soft directional key from upper-left; disable shadows and rely on the gradient textures for the illustrative shading.

authoredContext:
Many real-world situations can be represented by ellipses, including orbits of planets, satellites, moons and comets, and shapes of boat keels, rudders, and some airplane wings. A medical device called a lithotripter uses elliptical reflectors to break up kidney stones by generating sound waves. Some buildings, called whispering chambers, are designed with elliptical domes so that a person whispering at one focus can easily be heard by someone standing at the other focus. This occurs because of the acoustic properties of an ellipse. When a sound wave originates at one focus of a whispering chamber, the sound wave will be reflected off the elliptical dome and back to the other focus. See the figure. In the whisper chamber at the Museum of Science and Industry in Chicago, two people standing at the foci—about 43 feet apart—can hear each other whisper. When these chambers are placed in unexpected places, such as the ones inside Bush International Airport in Houston and Grand Central Terminal in New York City, they can induce surprised reactions among travelers.

Sound waves are reflected between foci in an elliptical room, called a whispering chamber.

An illustration of a semi-ellipsoidal dome with two focal points, F and F'. Blue lines with arrows represent rays originating from focal point F'. These rays reflect off the inner curved surface of the dome and converge at the second focal point F, demonstrating the reflective property of an ellipse.

discrepancies: Default state shows only one bold ray with the other six dimmed to ~12% opacity, whereas the source figure shows a full fan of ~7 equally bold navy rays crisscrossing the dome; the signature crossing pattern is barely visible at a glance (an 'All rays' toggle and step 3 do restore it).

Camera elevation is noticeably higher than the source: the source is near eye-level so the dome reads as a tall half-dome over a thin ellipse of floor, while the render looks down onto a large elliptical floor and the dome appears squashed and secondary.

Arrowheads: the source places multiple arrowheads along each leg (clearly near the reflection points and near F), while the generated figure puts a single cone at each leg midpoint, weakening the directional read of the incoming/outgoing legs.

The source's layered cutaway edge (white/grey/blue concentric rim bands and the dark horizontal cornice band inside the dome) is only faintly approximated — the interior band and multi-layer rim are much less pronounced than in the original.
Rays in the source reach high on the dome wall with apexes near the crown, producing steep tall triangles; several generated rays hit lower and read flatter under the elevated camera.
evaluation.notes: A convincing half-ellipsoid whispering gallery with correct focus-to-focus reflection math, good colors and rich step/toggle/ray-selection/pulse interactions; the main shortfalls are a default single-ray state and a higher-than-source camera that together make the opening view read less like the original crisscrossing ray fan.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; the remaining issues are concrete rendering fixes — default all rays bold, lower the camera elevation, add multiple arrowheads per leg, and strengthen the cutaway rim banding.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded three-dimensional cutaway drawing of a domed room built as a half-ellipsoid on a circular base. The outer shell carries a blue-to-white gradient and is cut away at the front so the viewer looks into the interior, where the inner surface and the floor are shaded warm tan; a thick gray band forms the base slab beneath the floor. Two small dark points on the floor mark the foci, labeled F' on the left and F on the right. A fan of dark blue segments with arrowheads leaves F', rises at a range of angles to strike the inside of the curved dome at several separated points, and reflects back down, every one arriving at F. The paths cross one another mid-room, and no two share a bounce point. Drawing many distinct routes between the same pair of labeled points emphasizes that the convergence holds no matter which direction a ray sets out in. The illustration accounts for the acoustics of a whispering chamber, where a person speaking softly at one focus of an elliptical dome is heard clearly by a listener at the other.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axes: +X screen-right (major axis of the room), +Y up, +Z toward viewer (depth). Dome = upper half of an ellipsoid with semi-axes a=3.0 in X, c=3.0 in Z, b=2.0 in Y, centered at origin; floor is the disk y=0, x²/9+z²/9≤1. Shell drawn with ~0.08 thickness; the front half (z>0 region in front of the cut plane z≈+1.1) is removed so the interior is visible. Gray base slab: cylinder radius 3.15, height 0.45, centered at y=−0.22, color #57585a with a lighter top lip #8d8e90. Floor tan gradient #f2e2bf (near) to #dcc79b (far). Dome outer gradient: deep blue #1f6ab0 at the rim rising to pale blue #b9dcf2 then near-white #f4fbff at the crown; cut-rim highlight strip #ffffff/#e8f2fa. Dome inner surface tan #e3cfa4 with a darker tonal band #cdb888 running horizontally around the interior at about y=0.7. Foci lie in the vertical XY cross-section (z=0) of the ellipse x²/9+y²/4=1: focal distance sqrt(9−4)=2.236, so F' at (−2.236, 0.02, 0) and F at (+2.236, 0.02, 0), drawn as dark navy dots radius ~0.09. Labels 'F'' and 'F' in italic serif, ~0.35 units below/outside each dot. Rays: all seven lie in the z=0 vertical plane and are dark navy #1c4e80, line width ~3px, with a single solid arrowhead at the midpoint of each segment. Each ray leaves F' at an upward angle, hits the ellipse boundary at a point P, and returns to F; total path |F'P|+|PF| = 2a = 6 for every ray (the defining ellipse property). Use seven well-separated bounce points on the ellipse, roughly at parameter angles t = 25°, 55°, 80°, 100°, 125°, 150°, 168° measured counterclockwise from +X on x=3cos t, y=2sin t — giving bounces spread from the right shoulder, over the crown, to the left shoulder so the outbound and return legs cross in the middle of the room, matching the source's woven crossing pattern.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the dome as two nested half-ellipsoid meshes (outer with THREE.BackSide off, inner with side=BackSide so the interior is lit) plus a thin torus-like rim strip along the cut; use a vertical gradient via a ShaderMaterial or a 1D CanvasTexture mapped to Y for both the blue exterior and the tan interior. Cut away the front with a clipping plane (renderer.localClippingEnabled = true, THREE.Plane normal (0,0,-1) at z=1.1) applied to the shell materials only, so the floor and rays stay whole. Rays as Line2/LineSegments2 for constant screen-space width; arrowheads as small flat cone meshes or sprite triangles oriented along each segment. Hit-testing for click: use invisible fat cylinders along each outbound segment as raycast proxies. All-rays view draws all seven at full opacity; single-ray view dims the others to ~12% opacity rather than hiding them so the fan context is retained. Animation: a small emissive sphere per ray advancing along the polyline at constant speed with all pulses sharing one normalized time parameter (path length identical), so they visibly reconverge at F simultaneously; add a soft expanding ring pulse at F' on launch and at F on arrival. Keep labels as HTML/CSS2DRenderer overlays anchored to the focus dots so they stay upright while orbiting. Lighting: hemisphere light plus one soft directional key from upper-left; disable shadows and rely on the gradient textures for the illustrative shading.

discrepancies: The blue exterior shell is reduced to a thin crescent outline: in the source the translucent blue dome covers the upper ~40% of the front silhouette and the tan cutaway opening is a smaller lower window, whereas here the cut plane (z=1.1) removes almost all of the blue, leaving an overwhelmingly tan figure.

Dome proportions are flatter than the source — the source dome is roughly half as tall as it is wide with rays peaking near the crown, while the generated half-ellipsoid (a=3, b=2) plus the very low 9° eye height compresses the ray fan into the lower-middle, losing the distinctive tall 'tent' peak of the printed figure.

The interior shading of the source (a dark horizontal band/ledge on the inner wall and a clearly curved inner surface receding behind the rim) does not read; the interior reads as an almost flat tan wash, weakening the sense of a hollow room.

The floor ellipse in the source is a narrow, nearly edge-on ellipse with the foci close to the front rim; here the floor opens up much wider, so the foci sit far inside a broad tan disc rather than on a thin visible floor line.

Arrowheads are placed only at each leg midpoint; the source also shows arrowheads clustered near the bounce points/ends of several segments, giving the characteristic dense chevron look near the dome wall.
evaluation.notes: Conceptually excellent and richly interactive (step-through, ray isolation, path-length readout, pulse animation, elevation slider), but the visual match suffers: the blue dome shell is nearly cut away entirely, the dome is too flat, and the ray fan lacks the tall crown-reaching peak of the printed figure.
action_items: Move the cutaway plane further forward (or restrict clipping to the lower portion) so the blue outer shell remains as a broad translucent cap over the top of the dome, matching the source's blue/tan proportion.
Increase the dome's vertical semi-axis (or raise the ray bounce parameters toward the crown) so the ray fan reaches high into the dome and forms the source's tall crossing 'tent' pattern.
Restore the dark interior band/ledge on the inner dome and add depth shading so the interior reads as a curved hollow surface rather than a flat tan disc.
Lower the default floor opening (narrower visible floor ellipse) and add arrowheads near the bounce points as well as at midpoints to match the source's chevron density.
plan_action_items: Specify the cut geometry explicitly as 'front quarter removed, blue cap retained above the opening' so the shell/opening ratio matches the printed figure.
